pairs.difference: A: the whistle's barrel is pure orange and its disc and mouth holes go to pure red-orange, so its shadows only climb in chroma. The ring is warm-tinted and nearly lost in the lens, and the field bleaches to a pale lemon glow around the whistle. B: the whistle is a slightly dustier orange with a related burnt-orange shadow side, the ring stays a true neutral steel, and the yellow field is even.
pairs.fix: Dusty matte orange plastic whistle; shadow side a deeper burnt orange, not red. Neutral grey steel ring. Even yellow background with no pale glow around the object.

pairs.difference: A: the brass splits into gold lights and red-orange shadows in the lens, so the bell's interior and tube undersides run the same red as the cord and tassels. The tassels are pure red and the cyan field is at full neon strength. B: the brass reads as one coherent copper-orange mass, the red cord is a little deeper, and the turquoise field is softer with pale rays.
pairs.fix: Brass bugle in muted golden brown; shadows a darker brown-bronze, not red. Deep crimson cord, clearly a different color from the metal. Softer turquoise background.

pairs.difference: B: the trim and flower are bright saturated blue with vivid green leaves. The saturated orange floor meets a crimson wall, and the cup's white picks up orange in the lens, so hero and background are both loud. A: the rim and flower are a greyed powder blue with olive-toned leaves, the porcelain stays creamy off-white, and the background is one muted brick-red family with a dark wine shadow.
pairs.fix: Greyed powder-blue rim and flower, muted olive leaves on off-white porcelain. One muted brick-red background with no bright orange floor; shadow a deep wine red.

pairs.difference: B: the apples and the basket both collapse to one pure red-orange mass in the lens, with almost no separation between fruit and wicker. The rope handle is highlighted yellow and the lilac field glows pale. A: the apples and wicker sit in a deeper crimson and brown range, the deep purple wall is steadier, the napkin's green is firm, and the table shadow is a muted grey-olive rather than pink.
pairs.fix: Apples in deep natural red with some yellow-green near the stems. Basket in brown-tan wicker, clearly less red than the apples. Shadow on the table a muted grey, not pink or orange.

pairs.difference: A: the staves are a uniform saturated orange that pushes wood toward pure hue, and that orange spreads into the rail and deck; only the hoops give rest. B: the staves are a browner, varied wood running from red-brown to tan, the deck is pale sandy wood, and the shadow goes to a muted brown-mauve.
pairs.fix: Barrel staves in natural brown oak, varied plank to plank from tan to red-brown, not orange. Pale weathered deck. Shadows a muted grey-brown.

pairs.difference: B: the body is a more orange, more uniform yellow and the rays are a deeper saturated blue. The road turns warm brown-mauve in the lens and the bumper is a warm grey, so few true neutrals remain. A: the asphalt holds a cool blue-grey, the chrome reads as neutral with sky reflected in it, the seats are a local brown, and the paint splits into yellow and ochre.
pairs.fix: Taxi paint in muted ochre-yellow with ochre shadows, not orange. Cool neutral grey asphalt. Bright chrome reflecting the blue sky.

pairs.difference: A: the tent carries a saturated orange flap and trim against bright yellow canvas, and the grass is neon yellow-green with yellow flowers. The sky and trees add blue and teal, so there is no quiet zone and hero and background are equally loud. B: the tent is one muted ochre mass with a brown shadow side, the forest falls to dull greens and red-browns, and only the foreground grass stays bright.
pairs.fix: Tent in one muted ochre canvas color with a brown shadow side and no orange trim. Quieter forest in dull greens and browns, softer grass, no flowers.

pairs.difference: A: the logs and ground are saturated orange that fills the card in the lens, and firelight spreads orange over the pot's belly and stones. Saturated stew and fire plus a teal sky gap keep the warm side loud, though the iron pot gives dark neutral rest. B: the logs are a browner orange, the ground a tan dirt, the pot a true grey, and the forest a calmer green, with red confined to the base of the pot.
pairs.fix: Logs in natural brown bark and tan dirt ground, not orange. Keep the iron pot and stones neutral grey, with orange firelight only right next to the flames.

pattern: Generated cards push local color toward pure hue: leather, wood, brass and off-white plastic all drift to saturated orange or cream, where real cards keep tan, brown, grey and true neutrals. Neutrals get warmed, so metal, whites, asphalt and stone lose their grey and little is left to rest the eye. Shadows climb in chroma to red-orange instead of a darker related color, and hero and background sit at equal loudness. Extra hues and glowing halos around the subject add to this, and in the lens the object collapses into one or two hot masses.
